notes: A multi-stage rest-api-service task. The repo ships a broken starter server (binds 127.0.0.1, /render runs user input through render_template_string = SSTI, routes lack validation/error codes, no JSON error handler), plus a source accounts CSV and an exporter. The agent must (1) repair/complete the Flask API to bind 0.0.0.0 on a fixed port, add exact JSON schemas, pagination and 404/400 JSON error bodies, and neutralize template rendering so /render echoes inputs ({{7*7}}, bold, empty) verbatim as text/plain; (2) keep a SQLite table, its /app/dump.csv export and the source CSV all identical; (3) run a local fixture server and fetch two raw byte payloads into /app/delivered byte-for-byte; (4) leave /app/server.out with the readiness line. The verifier boots the deliverable itself, probes it through 127.0.0.1 and the container IP, and drives hidden scenarios (fib values incl. k=90/200 and malformed k; block/tx confirmed/pending/not-found/invalid; paginated accounts with limit=0 and overshoot; SSTI/HTML/empty render payloads; unknown-route JSON 404). Difficulty derives from dependent_stages (server + DB + CSV export + remote fetch + boot log must all coexist and stay consistent), interaction_statefulness (long-running background service queried over the network after boot), adversarial_inputs (template-injection and malformed-parameter payloads), and debugging_ambiguity (each defect in the starter is silent until the verifier's hidden route probes).
